title: Legal redlines scratchpad - Riley Thompson
content:
Quick scratchpad for recurring clauses we flag in customer contracts / partner agreements. Mostly reminders and suggested negotiation language. Informal - notes to self and items to sync with Sales, Solutions, and Security teams.

Top-level priorities:
- Limit liability / cap. Aim for reciprocal cap tied to total fees (12 months) OR flat $XM for enterprise (placeholder). Carve out gross negligence and willful misconduct. Ask for waiver of consequential damages except for IP infringement.
- Indemnity: Keep narrow (IP infringement) and remove broad third-party claims tied to customer data unless caused by Redwood. Avoid broad indemnity to cover customer product claims.
- Data use & training license: No open license to train models on customer data. If customer data is used for model improvement, require opt-in and anonymization + explicit scope + retention limits.
- Ownership / outputs: Customer owns their input and any customer-provided fine-tuned models. Outputs: define permitted use + no ownership transfer of Redwood model weights or training data.
- Security / breach notifications: 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches, include scope, mitigation steps, and contact. Require SOC2 Type II or equivalent attestation; include right to provide summary of third-party audits rather than full reports.
- Subprocessors / vendors: Customer-facing list + 30-day notice for new subprocessors. Option for reasonable objection.
- Data retention & deletion: Define retention windows for logs, KV cache, and backup snapshots. Provide clear deletion obligations on termination and transition assistance (30-90 days).
- SLA & credits: Define measurable latency/availability SLOs, clear credit calculation. Avoid unlimited termination rights for intermittent breaches; include cure period (30 days). For hosted tiers, ensure credits capped and not sole remedy for availability issues.
- Termination & transition: On termination, preserve customer-managed data export for Y days and provide runbook for AWS/GCP export. For Private deployments, clarify handoff & support timeline.
- Export controls & compliance: Ensure customer remains responsible for their export compliance; Redwood to comply with applicable export laws.
- Audit rights: Use limited, scoped audit rights (remote review + compliance docs) rather than on-site audits. Require NDA for auditors.
- Confidentiality carveouts: Narrow exceptions for required disclosures (law enforcement) and for aggregated anonymized metrics.
- Pricing & overage: Cap sudden price increases; require 60-90 day notice for any pricing changes for committed capacity.
- Refunds / credits: For Dedicated reserved capacity, clarify billing overages vs committed units and define refund triggers (downtime beyond SLA).
- Model hallucination / output liability: Push to disclaimers - customer responsible for use of outputs; carveouts for willful misconduct. Add language that Redwood does not warrant accuracy of generated content.

Negotiation talking points (short bullets to use on calls):
- "We can accept a liability cap tied to fees (12 months) or a negotiated flat cap for enterprise, but we need mutuality and carveouts for gross negligence."
- "We can't grant a perpetual, royalty-free license to train on customer data - propose an opt-in data-improvement program with anonymization and explicit scope/duration."
- "For audits, we prefer remote reviews and attestations (SOC2) rather than on-site vendor audits."
- "SLA credits are the remedy for availability issues; termination should be a last resort after cure period for intermittent incidents."
- "For Dedicated/Private, be explicit about support windows and transition assistance fees if customer requests extended migration help."

Clause checklist (things to scan for in redlines):
- Broad IP indemnities or unilateral indemnity clauses
- Unlimited or uncapped liability for data loss or model outputs
- Unbounded license to use customer data for training
- Vague definitions of Confidential Information (ensure PII and customer data explicitly included)
- No breach notification timelines or inadequate security obligations
- Audit/on-site inspection rights without NDA/protections
- Ambiguous termination rights tied to convenience vs material breach
- Pricing change language without notice period for committed customers

People to loop depending on clause:
- Sales AE / AM (pricing, termination negotiations)
- Solutions Eng (technical feasibility: retention windows, KV cache deleting, on-prem export)
- Security/Privacy (SOC2, breach response, data residency, subprocessors)
- SRE / Infra (SLA definitions, metrics for latency/availability)
- Product (if feature changes requested to satisfy contract obligations)

Templates / suggested language snippets (very rough):
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct, the aggregate liability of each party for any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement will not exceed the amount of fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim, or $X, whichever is greater."
- Data-use: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train or improve its models without Customer's prior written consent. If Customer opts in, Redwood will (i) only use de-identified data, (ii) limit use to [scope], and (iii) retain data for no longer than [X months]."
- Breach notice: "Redwood will notify Customer of any Security Incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery, providing available information, mitigation steps, and remediation plan."

Open items / TODOs:
- Confirm dollar figure for enterprise liability cap ranges with Finance (TBD).
- Create short POS/one-pager for Sales describing our standard positions and acceptable concessions.
- Pull latest subprocessors list from privacy ops for appendix.
- Add a short checklist for Solutions Eng to include in scoping calls (retention, residency, KMS/HSM, export needs).

Recent rouges we've seen in redlines: vendor tried to insert broad license "to use, copy, modify, create derivatives" of customer content for any purpose - kill that or make extremely narrow for service ops.

Notes to self: keep this doc lean; maintain a Confluence page with canonical language and link it in sales playbook. Use JIRA-INF-3421 for tracking any contract exceptions requested this quarter.

-- riley
